body.p: S1000D® is an international specification for the procurement and production of technical publications (mainly used in aerospace and aviation industries). It is an XML-based specification for preparing, managing, and using equipment maintenance and operations information.

S1000D® has a modular architecture based on the following components:
Data Module - An XML-based, uniquely identified unit of information that can be managed, reused, and exchanged independently within the S1000D environment.
Data Module Structure - Describes the internal organization of a Data Module, typically divided into:
The Identification and Status part that identifies the Data Module within the CSDB structure.
The Content part that contains the detailed information of the Data Module.
Common Source DataBase (CSDB) - The managed repository where S1000D objects (such as Data Modules, Publication Modules, and illustrations) are stored, controlled, and related to each other. Publications are assembled from this repository.
Business Rules Exchange (BREX) - A specialized Data Module that defines project- or organization-specific business rules governing how S1000D is applied, and against which other Data Modules can be checked for conformance.
Publication Module (PM) - An XML-based control file that defines the structure, sequence, and inclusion of Data Modules in a deliverable publication, effectively acting as the publication's table of contents.
Information Control Number (ICN) - A unique identifier assigned to illustrations and other multimedia objects, allowing them to be managed and referenced as standalone entities within the CSDB.
Data Dispatch Note (DDN) - A control document used to describe, package, and manage the exchange of Data Modules and related S1000D objects between organizations or systems.
Data Module Requirement List (DMRL) - A structured list of required Data Modules for a project, used as a planning and tracking tool before and during authoring.
Comment - A Data Module type used to record review comments, feedback, or annotations that reference one or more existing Data Modules.

section.title: Built-in S1000D Support
section.p: includes built-in support for S1000D. You can work with S1000D issues 4.0, 4.1, 4.2, 5.0, 6, and 7 using built-in support for editing, visual authoring, templates, BREX handling, and smart paste.

section.title: Project Templates
section.p: You can start a new S1000D project for Issue 4.0, 4.1, 4.2, 5.0, 6, or 7 by using the project templates available in the S1000D category when you create a new project ( File New New Project ). Each template creates a bicycle-based sample project that you can adapt to your own product manually or with help from the AI assistant.

A project created from one of these templates includes:
Sample Data Modules, a Publication Module, a Data Management List, and illustrations (ICNs), all valid against the schemas for that issue.
The project's BREX and applicability objects (ACT, CCT, and PCT), grouped in the BREX & Applicability folder in the Project view.
Data Module, Publication Module, and other S1000D object templates for that issue, available in the S1000D [Issue x] category when you create new documents within the project.
A README.md file and an AI skill (in the .agents/skills folder) that describe the project and explain how to adapt it.

section.title: Default New Document Templates
section.p: You can use the provided file templates to create new S1000D® Data Modules or Publication Modules for issue 4.2. The templates are available when creating new documents from templatesnew documents from templates.

section.title: Author Mode Actions
section.p: S1000D documents can be edited in the Author visual editing mode, where you can switch between full-width and large-font styles. The following dedicated actions are available on the toolbar and in the S1000D menu when editing S1000D documents:

dlentry.dd: Inserts a reference to a data module (DM) or project module (PM).
Inserts a reference to an image (for example, CGM, PNG, or JPG) at the cursor position. You can optionally specify values for the Title, Width, Height, or Scale attributes.
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em01" (bold).
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em04" (overline).
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em05" (strikethrough).
Surrounds the selected text with a subscript element, used to insert a character (number, letter, or symbol) that appears slightly below the baseline and slightly smaller than the rest of the text.
Surrounds the selected text with a superscript element, used to insert a character (number, letter, or symbol) that appears slightly above the baseline and slightly smaller than the rest of the text.
Inserts a list item in the current list type.
Inserts a sequential list at the cursor position. A child list item is also inserted automatically by default.
Inserts a simple random (unordered) list at the cursor position. A child list item is also inserted automatically by default.
Inserts an unordered random list at the cursor position. A child list item is also automatically inserted by default.
Inserts a definition list at the cursor position. A child list item is also automatically inserted by default.
Opens a dialog box that allows you to configure and insert a table. You can generate a header and footer, set the number of rows and columns, and decide how the table is framed.
Inserts a new table row with empty cells below the current row. This action is available when the cursor is positioned inside a table.
Deletes the table row at the cursor position or multiple rows in a selection.
Inserts a new table column with empty cells after the current column. This action is available when the cursor is positioned inside a table.
Deletes the table column at the cursor position or multiple columns in a selection.
Joins the content of the selected table cells (both horizontally and vertically).
Splits the cell at the cursor location. If detects more than one option to split the cell, a dialog box is displayed where you can select the number of rows or columns to split the cell into.

section.p: The following legacy actions are available in the S1000D menu (but not on the toolbar):

dlentry.dd: Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em02" (italic).
Surrounds the selected text with an emphasis element with emphasisType="em03" (underline).

section.title: Floating Contextual Toolbar
section.p: Some of the most common S1000D Author mode actions are available on a dynamic floating toolbar that appears when you select content in supported locations within an S1000D document. The toolbar offers actions tailored to the current S1000D editing context.

section.title: Default Schema for Validation and Content Completion
section.p: The default schemas (issue 4.x, 5, 6, and 7) used for validation and content completion are stored in /frameworks/s1000d-base/ (with separate folders for each supported issue).

S1000D document editing features include schema-guided editing, validation, and content completion support. You can also view documentation for S1000D elements and attributes directly in the content completion window and in the Attributes view.

p.note: You can integrate support for other S1000D versions (such as 2.x or 3.x). For details, see .

section.title: Built-in Validation and Transformation Scenarios
section.p: includes various built-in validation and transformation scenarios for S1000D. There are built-in default validation scenarios for issues 4.0, 4.1, 4.2, 5.0, 6, and 7, CALS tables, and complete validation in categories for Data Modules, Publication Modules, and BREX.
Built-in transformation scenarios are available to convert data modules to PDF or HTML output, or to convert BREX modules to Schematron.

section.title: Publication Module Validation and Completeness Check
section.p: In addition to its other default S1000D validation scenarios, includes the S1000D PM Validation and Completeness Check scenario that validates a publication module, checks the completeness of the publication it defines, and validates the data modules included in the publication.

p.u: S1000D PM Validation and Completeness Check Scenario Validation Process:

ul.li: Validates the publication module against its schema, the BREX data module it declares, and the S1000D business rules.
Checks the publication module for completeness by following included publication modules and treating them as a single publication.

Validates each data module in the publication as it would be validated individually, using its associated validation scenarios or, if none are associated, the default validation scenarios for its document type. If the Report table layout problems setting is selected, the layout of tables is also checked.
Displays errors and warnings in the Results panel, where you can select an error to open the module at the problem location.

p.u: Examples of Problems Reported by the Completeness Check:

ul.li: References to data modules and publication modules that cannot be found.
BREX data modules declared by a module but not found.
References to a module that exists, but not in the issue or language specified by the reference (the available issues and languages are listed).
References with missing or incomplete codes.
Any referredFragment attributes whose ID is not in the referenced module.
ICNs that cannot be found.
External publications whose local files cannot be found and, when requested, remote locations that cannot be reached.
References to modules that are not part of the publication, when requested.
Data modules entered twice in the same publication module or in more than one publication module in the publication.
Publication modules entered within themselves.
Any pmRef references that point to a module that is not a publication module.
Modules that are not well-formed.
Documents that are not publication modules and publication modules whose folders cannot be listed.
Table layout problems, when requested.
Unexpected check failures, which are reported instead of causing the validation to fail.

section.p:
When you configure a validation engine for an S1000D validation scenario, the Configure Validation Engine dialog box contains the following options:
Include remote resources - Checks whether the remote HTTP(S) or (S)FTP locations of external publications can be reached. Disabled by default.
Report table layout problems - Checks the layout of CALS tables in the publication's data modules as they are read for the completeness check. Reports short rows, column and span mismatches, and incorrect column names. Enabled by default.
Validate references to modules outside the publication - Also looks up referenced modules that are not part of the publication, matching their issue and language and looking for the referred fragment within them. When disabled, these references are excluded from the check, and nothing is reported about them. Enabled by default.
Warn about references to modules not part of the publication - Reports each reference that resolves to a module outside the publication, helping keep a publication self-contained when intended. This option is independent of the preceding setting. Disabled by default.

section.title: BREX Editing, Validation, and Transformation
section.p: BREX modules can be edited in the Text or Author mode with content completion and validation support. You can validate S1000D documents directly against a BREX module (the schema type is automatically set to Schematron).
If a BREX module is referenced in the current S1000D document, automatically validates the file against the detected BREX.
Built-in BREX validation scenarios are available, including default scenarios for issues 4.0, 4.1, 4.2, 5.0, 6, and 7.

You can also convert BREX modules to Schematron using the built-in S1000D Brex To Schematron transformation scenario. This transformation also converts SNS (Standard Numbering System) rules (checking the data module code numbering against the SNS tree declared in the BREX) and notation rules (allowed and forbidden values).

section.title: Quick Fix Support
section.p: S1000D documents support some Quick Fixes. For example, a default Schematron rule checks whether the DM code is consistent with the file name in S1000D data modules. If a mismatch is detected, a Quick Fix option is available to automatically align the two.

section.title: Smart Paste
section.p: Content can be copied from web browsers or Word documents and pasted into S1000D documents while preserving structure and formatting.

section.title: Inserting References via Drag/Drop
section.p: You can drag Data Modules (DM), Publication Modules (PM), or Illustrated Content Numbers (ICN) into an S1000D document. The system will automatically generate the appropriate reference structure according to S1000D standards.

body.note: To display the CGM images that are commonly used in S1000D documents, you have to install the CGM Add-on.

section.title: Show Dependent and Referenced Resources
section.p:
You can view how S1000D files (DMC-, DME-, PMC-, DML-, UPF-) reference each other as a dependency graph. Right-click a file, then select one of the following actions:
Show referenced resources - Displays the resources referenced by the selected file.
Show dependent resources - Displays the resources that reference the selected file. Only references to files within the current project are resolved.

section.title: Find S1000D Resources
section.p: You can use the Open/Find Resource view to find S1000D data modules and publication modules based on the modules they reference. When the In content option is selected, a search for the code of a referenced module returns every module that contains a dmRef or pmRef reference to it. You can search for the code in the following forms:

ul.li: The data module code (for example: DMC-S1000DBIKE-AAA-D00-00-00-00AA-041A-A).

li.p: The code with the issue and language, as it appears in CSDB file names (for example: DMC-S1000DBIKE-AAA-D00-00-00-00AA-041A-A_001-00_EN-US).

ul.li: External data module references (DME-...) and publication module references (PMC-...).

section.p: A file is considered an S1000D module when its root element has an xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation attribute that starts with http://www.s1000d.org/S1000D. This is the same rule used by the S1000D framework.

A data module title in the search results is derived from the techName, infoName, and infoNameVariant elements in its dmTitle, separated by " - ". For example: Brake - Description - Front wheel. Missing parts are omitted. A publication module title is taken from its pmTitle.
The index is rebuilt automatically the first time starts after an update.

section.title: Commenting
section.p: Commented sections in S1000D modules can be collapsed or expanded using an inline toggle button that appears before the comment.

section.title: Publishing
section.p: Data Modules (DMs) can be published for preview in either PDF or HTML format. Any images referenced in the original files are preserved in the generated output.

ul.li: Use the S1000D Data Module PDF transformation scenario to generate PDF output for previewing.
Use the S1000D Data Module HTML transformation scenario to generate HTML output for offline preview in a web browser.

section.note: These transformation scenarios are provided for preview purposes only and are not designed for production.
